text:
Cornell University was founded on April 27, 1865, by Ezra Cornell and Andrew Dickson White, and was established as New York's land-grant institution. It was formally inaugurated on October 7, 1868, with 412 male students enrolling.
Cornell has developed as a technologically innovative institution, incorporating academic research into its campus infrastructure. It became one of the first electrified universities in 1883 and administers research and extension programs jointly funded by New York State and the U.S. federal government. Its main campus is located in Ithaca, New York, and features a mix of architectural styles. The university's endowment stands at $10.7 billion as of 2024. Cornell offers a wide range of programs, and its research activities are classified as "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity."
